questions.title: Planning and expressions
questions.question: A shop sells notebooks at R18 each. Input a whole number quantity from 0 to 20. Identify IPO (4), choose and justify types (4), write declared pseudocode with range validation (8), and give expected results for 0,20,21 and -1 (4).
questions.solution: Input quantity; process validation and quantity*18; output total or an error. Use INTEGER quantity and REAL or INTEGER total because this example uses whole rand. BEGIN, declare quantity and total, INPUT quantity, IF quantity < 0 OR quantity > 20 THEN OUTPUT Invalid ELSE SET total=quantity*18; OUTPUT total; ENDIF; END. Whole-number input is a stated assumption. Results: 0,360,invalid,invalid.
criteria: Multiplication and output with balanced blocks

questions.title: Selection and debugging
questions.question: Grades are Distinction for 75..100, Pass for 50..74, Revise for 0..49. Explain why testing >=50 before >=75 is wrong in an ELSEIF chain (4). Write the corrected chain including invalid input (10). Give outputs for -1,49,50,74,75,101 (6).
questions.solution: The broader >=50 condition catches distinctions before their branch can run. Reject mark < 0 OR mark > 100, then IF mark >=75 Distinction, ELSEIF mark >=50 Pass, ELSE Revise. Expected labels: invalid,Revise,Pass,Pass,Distinction,invalid.
criteria: Explains first matching branch and overlap
Correct ordered thresholds and final ELSE

questions.title: Loops and trace
questions.question: Read sales until -1, excluding it. Count only non-negative sales and total them. Other negative values display Invalid and are skipped. Write a complete algorithm (12). Trace 10,-5,0,20,-1 (4). Explain immediate -1 and why the update read must execute on every loop path (4).
questions.solution: Initialise total,count=0. Prime INPUT sale. WHILE sale<>-1: IF sale>=0 add to total and increment count ELSE OUTPUT Invalid ENDIF; INPUT sale; ENDWHILE. OUTPUT total,count. Trace after valid inputs: (10,1),(10,2),(30,3). -5 emits Invalid without changing totals. Final output 30,3. Immediate -1 outputs 0,0. The update read outside selection prevents invalid input being checked forever.

questions.title: Arrays and methods
questions.question: Write Highest(values,count) returning the highest of the first count meaningful items. Assume 1 <= count <= capacity (10). Show a call with [-4,-2,-9,999] and count 3 and state the result (4). Explain why highest=0 is wrong and what count=0 requires (6).
questions.solution: METHOD Highest(values AS REAL[],count AS INTEGER) RETURNS REAL; DECLARE highest REAL; DECLARE i INTEGER; SET highest=values[0]; FOR i=1 TO count-1; IF values[i]>highest THEN SET highest=values[i] ENDIF; ENDFOR; RETURN highest; ENDMETHOD. Call Highest(data,3) returns -2. 999 is unused. Zero is larger than every meaningful negative input and would invent a value. count=0 violates the contract and must be rejected or handled through an explicitly redesigned return/error contract.

questions.title: Design and object orientation
questions.question: Design a Book class for a library. Show a class diagram with private title and isBorrowed, a constructor and Borrow/ReturnBook operations (8). Describe two separate Book objects (4). Define encapsulation and explain the Book/Member association (4). Give normal and invalid-borrow tests (4).
questions.solution: Book fields -title:STRING,-isBorrowed:BOOLEAN; operations +Book(title:STRING),+Borrow():BOOLEAN,+ReturnBook(). Constructor sets title and FALSE. Borrow checks isBorrowed: return FALSE if already borrowed; otherwise set TRUE and return TRUE. Two NEW calls have independent state, so borrowing one does not borrow the other. Encapsulation restricts state changes to controlled operations. Member borrows Book through an association, not inheritance. First borrow succeeds; repeat borrow fails; returning then borrowing succeeds.
criteria: Correct class compartments and typed private fields

questions.title: Flowcharts and Boolean rules
questions.question: A discount applies when a customer is a member AND spends at least R500. Members and non-members may buy. Draw a labelled flowchart (8), write equivalent Boolean selection (6), and give the four combinations at spend 499/500 and member TRUE/FALSE (6).
questions.solution: Start, input membership and spend, decision member AND spend>=500, Yes output Discount, No output Standard price, End. Monetary spend is assumed non-negative. The four outcomes are FALSE/499 Standard, FALSE/500 Standard, TRUE/499 Standard, TRUE/500 Discount. IF member AND spend >= 500 THEN OUTPUT Discount ELSE OUTPUT Standard price ENDIF. Do not reject a non-member.

questions.title: Nested loops and matrices
questions.question: A 2 by 3 matrix contains rows [2,4,6] and [1,3,5]. Write pseudocode to display each row total (10), trace both totals (4), explain where to reset the accumulator and give the total number of additions (6). Treat this as written design if the tracer lacks matrix support.
questions.solution: Declare matrix[2][3], row,column INTEGER,rowTotal REAL and initialise the six cells. FOR row=0 TO1: SET rowTotal=0; FOR column=0 TO2: rowTotal=rowTotal+matrix[row][column]; ENDFOR; OUTPUT rowTotal; ENDFOR. Row0 totals 2,6,12; row1 totals1,4,9. Reset before each inner loop, otherwise second output becomes21. Six additions execute.

questions.title: Search sorting and associated data
questions.question: names=[Ada,Bo,Cy],marks=[65,90,70]. Trace descending bubble sort after each full pass, keeping names aligned (10). Search for Cy in the result and display the matching mark (6). Explain the mismatch caused by sorting only marks (4).
questions.solution: Pass1 compares65/90 then65/70, producing marks[90,70,65],names[Bo,Cy,Ada]. Pass2 compares90/70 and changes nothing. Cy is at index1 and marks[1]=70. Descending comparison swaps when left < right. Linear search visits Bo then Cy. Sorting marks alone would leave Ada incorrectly paired with90 and change the meaning of the records.

questions.title: Methods scope and overloading
questions.question: Write Cost(quantity,price) returning quantity*price (6). Write overloaded Cost(quantity,price,discountRate) returning the discounted total, with rate0..1 assumed (6). Show results for (3,20) and (3,20,0.1) (4). Explain argument matching and why local total should not be used directly by Main (4).
questions.solution: Cost(quantity AS INTEGER,price AS REAL) RETURNS REAL returns quantity*price. The three-parameter overload also accepts discountRate REAL and returns quantity*price*(1-discountRate). Results60 and54. Two versus three arguments select different signatures. A local total belongs to its method scope; return it and store the returned result in Main. Parameter names do not by themselves distinguish overloads.

questions.title: Integrated object design and tests
questions.question: Plan a Student report using private name/mark, a validating constructor and Result() returning Pass for mark>=50 (8). Give an algorithm to count passes across three students (6). Explain tests for49,50,100,101 and two students sharing a name (6).
questions.solution: Student has -name:STRING,-mark:REAL,+Student(name,mark),+Result():STRING. The constructor accepts only0..100 or reports failure through the stated design contract. Result returns Pass or Revise. Main creates three valid objects,initialises passed=0, loops over objects and increments when Result()=Pass, then outputs passed. 49 Revise;50 and100 Pass;101 rejected before valid object storage. Two objects may share a name but keep independent marks; use a unique ID if identity matters.
